chapter: Learning drums and Roy Eldridge's band
title: Frank Clarke and the school band at Herron Hill
summary: With bassist Frank Clarke and a teacher who requisitioned school instruments, he took a snare drum home and formed a little band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: And I met -- which I was just about 17, you know. I didn't have a job or anything. So there was a friend of mine in school named Frank Clarke who was a wonderful bassist, you know, and well we had a band at Herron Hill, so we had a -- oh, what's his name? He was an Irish fellow. He taught Ray Brown and all those bass players from Pittsburgh.
Really? Well, does Ray Brown come from Pittsburgh?
What was his name? I should never forget his name.
And he was an Irish fellow, but he could play all of the instruments, and he began to let us take instruments home, and then we formed a little band, you know, in
Did he have a little money, that he owned these different instruments?
No, he would requisition them from the school. And tell us to be careful and so forth, and don't break the instruments, and -- oh, if I could just think of his name.
Well, it'll come to you. Maybe overnight it'll come to you.
And you can tell me tomorrow. We'll put it on. Fancy that. So what did you take home?
Well, I took the snare drum home.
